as_of_line: As of 13:50 Prague time, 2 November. The statuses update as the work moves.
headline: What's being built today
intro: Thirteen pieces of work, run by AI agents working in parallel, with Alex steering. First comes the tooling that lets the agents work on their own. Then come ten demos of what a GTM engineer builds, and they all end up on this site.

how_it_runs.text: Alex wrote a project charter in the morning: the goal, the rules every agent follows, and the list of deliverables.

how_it_runs.lead: One agent per piece of work.
how_it_runs.text: Each deliverable gets its own spec, a plan an agent can carry out on its own, and its own background Claude Code session. The sessions run at the same time and message each other.
Any agent that needs Alex sends its question to the "answer desk", a single window that shows him one question at a time.
Anything that needs Alex (recordings, decisions, sign-offs) happens while he's at the computer today. The rest builds overnight, and a cleanup session follows tomorrow morning.

tooling.what: Sets up a working folder, instructions and a background session for every other piece.
tooling.status: Running. Folders for every demo created at 13:45.

tooling.what: Decides with Alex what gets researched and how deep, so the agents work from findings instead of guesses.
tooling.status: Spec written, Alex's answers in. Starts after bootstrap.

tooling.what: Keeps the plan consistent: adds deliverables and updates everything that depends on them.
tooling.status: Spec written. Runs in the main orchestration session.

demos.what: Scraping and researching prospects at scale. It goes first, because other demos use what it finds.
Deep research on the company and the people likely to be involved in hiring.
demos.status: Alex is doing this one himself.

demos.what: 10 ideal customer profiles, each with its own drip sequence, and a classifier that sends each lead to the right one. The first message is personalized before import. Shown as a video clipped from these recordings.
15 minutes of Alex talking turns into a near-finished blog post. He does the last 10%.
Three posts made with that pipeline, on the ideas behind this project.
Pixel-perfect, on-brand visual templates for LinkedIn.
LinkedIn posts written in the company's own voice.
A page for each key stakeholder, and a running picture of the project.
An agent that watches the recordings and tells the website what to add. This section is its first post.
Alex designing in Canva, on camera, near the end of the day.

after_how_it_runs.text: Think of it like the expensive movie actor. They fly him out to the scene, they shoot all of his scenes first, even if it's not in chronological order of the movie, because his time is the most expensive.
after_how_it_runs.source: Alex, S03 at 11:11 (11:36 Prague), on why everything that needs him is done first

after_demos.text: Without being prompted, it should see all this stuff being built and say, okay, these are the deliverables. Let's find a way to put the deliverables on the website so people kind of know what to expect.
after_demos.source: Alex, S04 at 08:23 (12:24 Prague), describing the legibility analyzer
